context: Introduction to the Fedora translation mailing list. Polished; Arvind uses AI as a drafting tool for this register, then edits.
brief: Write an introduction email to the Fedora translators mailing list: you're a native Norwegian speaker new to Fedora translation, you finished the systemd Bokmål translation on Weblate, you'd like reviewer access without stepping on the coordinator's toes, and you disclose that you use AI as a drafting aid but review everything yourself.
text:
Hei,

I'm Arvind Froiland, (arvindfroi). I'm a native Norwegian speaker and fairly new to Fedora translation, so I figured I'd introduce myself.

A little while back I finished the Norwegian Bokmål translation of systemd on Weblate (all 285 strings), and I'd like to keep going. There's plenty more I can take on across the core packages, and I'd also like to help keep the existing Norwegian translations in good shape rather than letting them drift.

I saw that Kjartan is the coordinator for Norwegian - I'm not looking to step on anyone's toes, I just want to pitch in properly. If it's possible to add me to the Norwegian team as a reviewer so I can approve and fix translations directly instead of only leaving suggestions, that would help a lot. Happy to start with whatever scope you're comfortable with.

On process: I do use AI as a drafting aid, but I read through everything myself as a native speaker before it goes in, and I'll follow whatever the team prefers here.

Thanks, and looking forward to working with you.

Arvind

context: Second, warmer version of the Fedora mailing list introduction. Polished; likely AI-drafted, human-edited.
brief: Write a friendly introduction to the Fedora translators list: greet in Norwegian, explain you've been doing open source translation and finished all 285 systemd Bokmål strings, offer to help with core packages, ask about reviewer access respectfully, and disclose your AI drafting workflow.
text:
Hei everyone,

My name is Arvind (arvindfroi). I'm Norwegian and I've been doing a fair bit of open source translation lately, so I figured it was about time I said hello here properly instead of just lurking around Weblate.

I recently sat down and finished the Norwegian Bokmål translation for systemd - all 285 strings - and honestly I had a good time doing it, so I'd like to keep going. There's a lot more I can pick up across the core stuff (Anaconda, dnf and friends), and I'd also like to help keep the Norwegian we already have from going stale.

I see Kjartan is the coordinator for Norwegian, and I don't want to step on any toes - he's been doing this far longer than me. I'd just like to actually pull my weight. If it's possible to get added to the Norwegian team as a reviewer so I can approve and fix things directly rather than only leaving suggestions, that would make a real difference. Totally fine to start small and earn it.

One thing I want to be upfront about: I do use AI as a drafting tool, but I'm a native speaker and I read and fix everything myself before it goes anywhere - I'm not in the business of dumping machine output on anyone. Happy to work however the team prefers.

Anyway, that's me. Looking forward to helping out.

Arvind

context: Email to an open-source maintainer about a translation PR. Polished, technically detailed; likely AI-assisted draft.
brief: Write to the PPSSPP maintainer about your pull request updating the Norwegian Bokmål translation: ~950 new strings, coverage from 28% to 92%, existing translations kept, technical terms untouched, placeholders verified, and disclose AI-assisted translation reviewed by you as a native speaker.
text:
Hi Henrik,

I'm a native Norwegian speaker and recently started contributing to open source. I've opened a pull request with a large update to the Norwegian (Bokmål) translation (assets/lang/no_NO.ini).

It fills in around 950 previously untranslated strings, bringing Norwegian coverage from roughly 28% to about 92%. I kept all existing translations, left genuinely technical terms (OpenGL, Vulkan, shader names, etc.) untouched, and verified that every key, placeholder (%1, %s, ...) and Alt-key hotkey (&) matches en_US.ini exactly.

Disclosure per your AI policy: the new strings were translated with AI assistance (Claude) and reviewed by me as a native speaker, and I take full responsibility for the content. This is also noted in the PR description.

Happy to adjust anything you'd like. Thanks for all your work on PPSSPP!

Best,
Arvind

context: Heartfelt request to Anthropic to extend an open-source maintainer program. Possibly AI-polished but personal in content.
brief: Write to the Anthropic team asking them to extend or renew the open-source maintainer program: be upfront that you don't code, explain you contribute through translation and localization with Claude's help, say you're worried about losing momentum, and thank them.
text:
Hi Anthropic Team,
I'm writing to ask if there is any chance you might extend the open-source maintainer program, or perhaps renew it for next year.
To be completely upfront, I don't know how to code. For a long time, I thought that meant I couldn't really participate in the open-source community. But recently, I've found a niche contributing through translation and localization, and Claude has been incredibly helpful in making that happen.

Using Claude allows me to understand the context and subtle nuances of different projects, giving me the confidence to actually contribute to multiple repositories. It has opened up a whole side of tech that I thought was closed off to me.

Right now, I feel like I'm just getting started and finally finding my footing. I'm really worried about losing access and missing out on this momentum just as things are beginning to click.

Would you consider extending the current period or renewing it for the upcoming year? Having a bit more time would mean a lot to contributors like me who are trying to help out through non-traditional avenues.
Thanks so much for your time and for building such a useful tool.

Best,
Arvind

context: Innledning til gruppeoppgave i ORG219 (strategisk ledelse). NB: gruppearbeid — kun deler av dokumentet er Arvinds egen tekst, og teksten kan være AI-assistert.
brief: Skriv en innledning til en akademisk oppgave om forskjellene mellom private og offentlige virksomheter og hvordan de påvirker relevansen av skoleretninger i strategisk ledelse, med helsesektoren som gjennomgående eksempel.
text: I denne oppgaven gjør vi rede for hva som kjennetegner forskjellene mellom private og offentlige virksomheter, og diskuterer hvordan disse forskjellene påvirker relevansen av sentrale skoleretninger og teorier i strategisk ledelse. Vi tar utgangspunkt i designskolen, planleggingsskolen, posisjoneringsskolen, ressursbasert teori og dynamisk kapabilitetsteori. For å gjøre diskusjonen mest mulig konkret bruker vi helsesektoren som gjennomgående eksempel, ettersom den i norsk sammenheng inneholder både statlig eide sykehus og private tilbydere, og dermed gir et godt grunnlag for å sammenligne på tvers av styringsform. Oppgaven er bygget opp ved at vi først redegjør for forskjellene mellom sektorene på et mer overordnet nivå, før vi drøfter relevansen til hver skoleretning for seg.

context: Utdrag fra personlige eksamensnotater i statsvitenskap (ST-200). Hierarkiske punktlister, fete nøkkelbegreper, blanding av norsk fagspråk og engelske begreper.
brief: Skriv eksamensnotater som oppsummerer McDonnells (2020) artikkel om kommunestørrelse og politisk deltakelse, i punktliste-stil med fete nøkkelbegreper.
text:
Artikkelen tar utgangspunkt i den klassiske ideen om at lokaldemokrati er en «treningsarena for demokrati», der vanlige borgere kan lære om politikk og oppleve at de har innflytelse.

Det går tilbake til Dahl som så lokalstyret som en motvekt til et fjernt og profesjonalisert nivå.

Hovedspørsmålet i artikkelen er derfor: Hvordan påvirker kommunestørrelse (innbyggertall) politisk effektivitet og politisk deltakelse på lokalt nivå?

Konklusjonen hans er klar:
- Borgere i små kommuner føler seg mer politisk effektive, og deltar mer i lokalpolitikken, enn borgere i store kommuner.

Begrepet «efficacy»: Borgernes subjektive følelse av mestring, kompetanse og påvirkningskraft.

Artikkelen skiller mellom 2 typer forklaringer i deltakelse:
- Demand side
  - Individuelle ressurser, motivasjon, sosiale nettverk osv
- Supply side
  - Institusjonelle rammer og konteksten borgerne møter, f eks kommunestørrelse, organisering, politisk system

2 konkurrerende teorier: Small is beautiful vs Large is lively
- Small is beautiful
  - Jo mindre kommune, jo høyere intern og ekstern politisk efficacy og dermed mer deltakelse
  - Politikken er nær, konkret og oversiktlig, da saker gjelder hverdagsnære ting og er lite komplekse
  - Hver stemme teller mer i små kommuner
- Large is lively
  - Jo større kommune, jo mer deltakelse, særlig valgdeltakelse, partipolitikk osv
  - Større kommuner har større oppgaver og mer viktige saker → vekker mer interesse

Small is beautiful får mye empirisk støtte, mens large is lively får ingen empirisk støtte
